LG B6 OLED TV Review: A Solid Entry-Level Choice Facing Stiff Competition

28 Oct 2026, 12:26 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Tech Desk · Source: www.wired.com

Key takeaways Overview of the LG B6 The LG B6 has entered the market as the brand's entry-level OLED television. While it maintains the ultra-thin physical profile synonymous with OLED technology—measuring just a quarter-inch at the top—it faces a landscape of evolving display tech

Overview of the LG B6

The LG B6 has entered the market as the brand's entry-level OLED television. While it maintains the ultra-thin physical profile synonymous with OLED technology—measuring just a quarter-inch at the top—it faces a landscape of evolving display technology, including emerging RGB televisions and specialized art-focused displays.

Performance and Display

Testing reveals that the B6 excels in rendering deep blacks and detailed gray textures, providing high clarity in dark film sequences. However, the television exhibits limitations in peak brightness and contrast compared to higher-end models. During stress tests involving high-contrast scenes, the B6 struggled to render background details that remain visible on more premium displays. While color reproduction is generally competent, specifically regarding skin tones, saturation levels may appear muted compared to newer RGB competitors.

For gaming, the B6 offers a 120-Hz refresh rate, providing responsive motion handling. In real-world testing with PC titles, visual output remained sharp and fluid.

Software and User Experience

The B6 utilizes LG’s proprietary WebOS interface. Setup is streamlined through the LG ThinQ app, allowing quick integration of major streaming services. The television includes several software-driven features, such as an AI picture enhancement mode and an optional subscription-based 'Gallery+' artwork mode.

Users should note that the included remote may present usability challenges. The remote features a pointer function that cannot be permanently disabled, and the layout of buttons, including the unlit app shortcuts, can be difficult to navigate in low-light environments.

Connectivity and Physical Design

The unit is equipped with four HDMI ports, all supporting 120-Hz, alongside optical audio, two USB 2.0 ports, and a LAN port. Notably, the hardware relies on Wi-Fi 5, rather than more current wireless standards.

Market Context

As an entry-level offering, the B6 provides many features typical of flagship sets but is positioned in a crowded market. Prospective buyers may find that LG's own C6 model, often available for a relatively small price increase, offers significant improvements in brightness and overall contrast. Before purchasing, consumers are encouraged to weigh the cost-to-performance ratio against alternative models like the LG C5 or competing RGB televisions.

Readers can find technical specifications and further manufacturer details at the official source: https://www.wired.com/review/lg-b6/.
